extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: LongBench is the first bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding, comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in both English and Chinese. It contains 4,750 test instances with an average length of 6,711 words (English) and 13,386 characters (Chinese), covering single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. All datasets are standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of large language models.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai; Xin Lv; Jiajie Zhang; Hongchang Lyu; Jiankai Tang; Zhidian Huang; Zhengxiao Du; Xiao Liu; Aohan Zeng; Lei Hou; Yuxiao Dong; Jie Tang; Juanzi Li
extraction.citeAs: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li. LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv:2308.14508v2, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench was assembled by combining three approaches: (1) directly extracting data from existing public datasets (6 datasets), (2) building and processing data based on existing public datasets to suit long context evaluation (10 datasets), and (3) manually creating and annotating new data (5 datasets). For the manually curated MultiFieldQA datasets, documents were collected from multiple sources including legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, and academic papers, and three Ph.D. students annotated question-answer pairs. For multi-doc QA, complete Wikipedia passages were used to extend existing multi-hop QA datasets. Synthetic tasks were constructed by randomly sampling passages from Wikipedia and the C4 dataset, with summaries generated using GPT-3.5-Turbo. Code completion datasets were sampled from GitHub repositories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Web Scraping; Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source datasets and repositories include: NarrativeQA (literature and film), Qasper (NLP papers), HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue (Wikipedia-based multi-hop QA), DuReader (Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao), GovReport (U.S. Government Accountability Office and Congressional Research Service reports), QMSum (meeting transcripts), MultiNews (news articles), VCSUM (Chinese meeting recordings), TREC (web questions), TriviaQA (Wikipedia and web), SAMSum (messenger-like dialogues), LSHT (Chinese news), English Wikipedia passages, C4 dataset (Chinese sections), LCC (GitHub code files), RepoBench-P (GitHub repositories). MultiFieldQA documents sourced from Arxiv, C4 Dataset, WuDaoCorpora, Chinese Judgements Online, Wikipedia, and Chinese Government Website.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three Ph.D. students with extensive NLP research experience annotated question-answer pairs for the MultiFieldQA datasets (English and Chinese). Annotators were asked to propose one question and a ground-truth answer for each document, with requirements that questions be clear with definitive and relatively short answers, evidence paragraphs be randomly distributed throughout the article, and questions cover varied types (information-extracting, summarizing, multi-hop reasoning). Answers were required to be inferable from the documents. Average annotation time was approximately 5 minutes per sample.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Cross-validation among annotators showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in NLP
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo (used to generate summaries of passages for PassageRetrieval-en and PassageRetrieval-zh synthetic tasks)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Memorization bias: datasets derived from Wikipedia (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue) may yield relatively high scores without context because prevalent LLMs are likely trained on Wikipedia; annotation bias mitigated by randomizing placement of evidence paragraphs to avoid answer-related statements clustering at the beginning or end
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic evaluation metrics (ROUGE-L, F1) may not accurately reflect response quality and may underestimate models that generate longer responses; performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities, not purely long-context modeling ability; summarization and code completion tasks are not sufficiently discriminating due to insensitivity of similarity-based metrics; simply averaging over all tasks may not be a good indicator of long context capability since more discriminating tasks (e.g., synthetic tasks) may dominate final rankings
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating large language models' long context understanding capabilities across multiple tasks and languages; benchmarking multi-task bilingual long context understanding; studying model performance across varying context lengths; serving as a testbed for future research in long context modeling
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For multi-document QA datasets (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue), supporting passages were included within the context and distracting passages were added until the total length reached a maximum length, then passages were randomly ordered to form the multi-document context. For DuReader, several documents related to the question plus arbitrarily selected distractor documents were combined until each question was associated with 20 documents. For few-shot learning datasets (TREC, LSHT, SAMSum, TriviaQA), a random number of examples was sampled from the training set and concatenated to form the context. For PassageRetrieval tasks, 30 passages were randomly sampled and one was summarized using GPT-3.5-Turbo to create the query. For PassageCount, passages were randomly selected from Wikipedia, each repeated a random number of times, and then shuffled. For RepoBench-P, cross-file code snippets including the gold snippet were shuffled and combined into context. For LongBench-E, uniform sampling based on length was applied to obtain a more even distribution across length ranges of 0-4k, 4k-8k, and 8k+.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was extracted from test sets of public datasets to avoid test leakage, with the exception of VCSUM. Two extraction strategies were used: random sampling (to maintain natural length distribution for LongBench) and uniform sampling by length (for LongBench-E). For TriviaQA few-shot examples, passages with fewer than 1,000 words were filtered out. For MultiNews, 'Document i' labels were prepended to each article and articles were concatenated into context. All 21 datasets were standardized into a unified format with consistent (I, C, A) structure. When input length exceeded a model's maximum context length during evaluation, the input sequence was truncated from the middle.
